descriptor: Regulated Electric & Gas Utilities (Energy Networks / European Grid Operator) · reported in EUR

charts.title: Revenue & YoY Growth
charts.annotation: Revenue drops ~3x from FY2015 to FY2016 because E.ON deconsolidated Uniper (the conventional generation and global commodities business) in a 2016 spin-off -- not an operating decline. The restated ex-Uniper comparatives live only in the kpis table.

charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
EBITDA & EBITDA Margin
charts.annotation: The FY2016 step-down is the Uniper spin-off (deconsolidation), not a margin collapse -- compare periods either side of FY2016 with caution.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

charts.title: Cash vs Total Debt vs Economic Net Debt
Adjusted EBITDA by Segment
charts.annotation: Only FY2024 and FY2025 are disclosed on this segment basis.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For E.ON SE: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted) and economic net debt -- E.ON's own leverage metric, which adds pension and hybrid-capital adjustments the statutory debt figure misses.

For E.ON SE: economic net debt has run well above statutory total debt less cash every period shown; the DCF's net-debt bridge uses the statutory balance-sheet figures at the latest balance date, not this management metric.

What to watch:

  • Economic net debt trend versus Adjusted EBITDA (the grid business carries structurally high leverage against regulated, stable cash flows)
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

segmentEbitda.title: Adjusted EBITDA by segment
segmentEbitda.content:
E.ON reports Adjusted EBITDA across four segments: Energy Networks (the regulated electricity and gas grids), Energy Infrastructure Solutions, Energy Retail (customer supply), and Corporate/Other.

For E.ON SE: Energy Networks generated roughly 78% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA (€7,695m of €9,849m group total) -- E.ON is overwhelmingly a regulated grid operator, with Retail and Infrastructure Solutions as smaller, more competitive supplements. Only FY2024 and FY2025 are disclosed on this segment basis.

What to watch:

  • Networks' share of group EBITDA (regulatory allowed-return changes move the whole group)
  • Retail margin volatility versus Networks' stability

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For E.ON SE: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For E.ON SE: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For E.ON SE: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For E.ON SE: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For E.ON SE: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For E.ON SE: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For E.ON SE: the FY2015-to-FY2016 drop (€116bn to €38bn) is the 2016 Uniper spin-off deconsolidating conventional generation and global commodities trading, not an operating collapse -- do not read the YoY line across that boundary. The growth rate since FY2016 is the comparable series; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth since FY2016
  • Whether growth is organic, acquired, or regulatory (allowed network revenue resets)
  • Interim rows show seasonality (gas/heating demand is winter-weighted)

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For E.ON SE: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
